title: A Holy Air Is Breathing Round
description: A Holy Air Is Breathing Round in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 157, “One in Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A Ho-ly air is breath-ing round, A fra-grance from a-bove; Be ev-ery soul from sense un-bound, Be ev-ery spi-rit love.

lines: A Holy air is breathing round,
Be every soul from sense unbound,
O God, unite us heart to heart,
That we be never drawn apart,
And love not Thee nor Thine;
But, by the cross of Jesus taught,
Be nearer to each other brought,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
